name: Financial
scope: Private finance / business-sector treatment of UAP (or UAP disclosure) as a financial risk or opportunity: investment managers, funds, banks, insurers/reinsurers, rating agencies, auditors, corporate risk functions, standards bodies, and market regulators in a market-supervision capacity.
excludes: Government appropriations / power of the purse (Legislative/Government), defense-contractor budgets (Military/Government), academic/scientific funding (Scientific), and novelty products (alien-abduction certificates, meme coins, prediction-market bets).
method: First-principles ladder ordered by increasing legal accountability, capital at risk, and cost of reversal. Non-ontological: rungs measure the sector's acts (recognizing, disclosing, pricing, allocating, insuring), never the nature of the phenomenon. Crediting a financial act (e.g. an ETF) does not endorse its investment thesis.
insight: Zero Partial — and that matters. Finance moves in binary thresholds, not gradual capabilities: an ETF exists or it doesn't; a risk factor is in the filing or it isn't. So there is no 'in-progress' state. The consequence is a threshold-and-herding sector: when a real trigger lands, finance won't climb the rungs gradually like science — it will cross them in a cascade, as each institution copies the first mover. This could go from 3 green to 8 green in months. That is exactly why preparation is urgent: the day it flips, it is already too late.
summary: Finance has produced three isolated but concrete acts — a regulated UAP risk disclosure and an operating UAP-disclosure ETF, plus the recognition they imply. The analytical infrastructure beneath is almost entirely absent: no internal risk governance, no quantitative pricing, no insurance or risk transfer, no ratings or standards treatment, and no market-wide adoption. A few pioneers have moved; the serious institutional market has not.
sourcingQuality: Strong — SEC EDGAR filings and official Cboe/fund records. (Two other AI passes wrongly reported 'all Not yet'; they failed to search EDGAR. The Procure and UFOD events are real and primary-sourced.)

rungs.title: Formal financial recognition
rungs.oneLiner: A regulated manager names UAP as a financial risk. e.g. Procure Space ETF (UFO) risk factor, SEC.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Minimum positive financial act — a named institution puts UAP into its formal financial vocabulary. Nothing yet governed, priced or hedged.
rungs.statusRationale: A regulated manager has formally identified UAP as a financial risk in a securities-law document. Discrete threshold, crossed and irreversible.

sources.label: Procure Space ETF (UFO) prospectus — SEC Rule 497 supplement, 8 June 2021
Procure Space ETF prospectus, 28 Feb 2026 (UAP risk factor retained)

rungs.limitation: Inherited from the regulated disclosure at rung 3; not double-counted.

skepticChallenge.challenge: One niche space ETF whose ticker was already UFO.
skepticChallenge.holds: Limits significance, not the existence threshold; breadth is measured at rung 8.

rungs.title: Internal risk ownership & exposure mapping
rungs.oneLiner: No bank/insurer/fund with a named UAP risk owner or mapped exposure on record.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Recognition becomes operational when someone inside an institution owns the exposure and maps affected assets/counterparties.
rungs.statusRationale: No public record of any bank, insurer, asset manager or corporation assigning a named UAP risk owner, adding UAP to an enterprise-risk register, or mapping exposure. A prospectus risk factor governs the filing, not a dedicated UAP risk-management capability.

rungs.title: Regulated exposure disclosure
rungs.oneLiner: A UAP risk factor sits in an SEC-filed prospectus, retained to 2026. e.g. Procure Space ETF.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Recognition becomes public and legally consequential — management stands behind wording in a securities-law-governed document.
rungs.statusRationale: A UAP risk factor is stated in an SEC-filed prospectus and retained across editions (2021 to 2026), warning that operational/cyber/data-security interference with satellites could reduce portfolio value.

sources.label: Procure Space ETF prospectus (UAP risk factor), SEC-filed 2021 & 2026

skepticChallenge.challenge: The SEC just received the filing; it didn't validate the risk.
skepticChallenge.holds: Correct re the SEC — this is an issuer/manager act, not SEC endorsement. The rung measures regulated disclosure by a market participant, which is satisfied.

rungs.title: Quantified exposure & explicit pricing
rungs.oneLiner: No probability, loss estimate, sensitivity, or UAP-specific risk premium published.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Qualitative language says something might matter; quantification assigns probabilities, scenario values, sensitivities, premiums, spreads — a testable model.
rungs.statusRationale: No institution publicly assigns numbers to UAP exposure. Near miss: the UFOD ETF selects 'disclosure beneficiary' stocks but discloses no probability-weighted scenario, UAP valuation factor, or measurable sensitivity — thematic selection is not pricing the event.

rungs.title: Dedicated capital allocation / investable product
rungs.oneLiner: An exchange-listed product allocates capital on a UAP thesis. e.g. UFOD ETF, Cboe, Feb 2026.
rungs.firstPrinciples: The sector commits real investor capital via a regulated product, with fiduciary and regulatory obligations.
rungs.statusRationale: A regulated, exchange-listed product actively allocates investor capital around a UAP-disclosure thesis. Discrete threshold, crossed.

sources.label: Tuttle Capital UFO Disclosure ETF (UFOD) — Cboe BZX listing, trading from 5 Feb 2026
UFOD official fund data (inception, ~$2.82M net assets, 61 holdings, 22 Jul 2026)
To The Stars Academy Regulation A offering (~$1.09M by Apr 2018), SEC-filed — earlier supporting capital-formation event

rungs.limitation: UFOD's own materials make aggressive nonhuman/reverse-engineering claims. Crediting the financial act (capital was allocated around the thesis) does NOT endorse the thesis.

skepticChallenge.challenge: Tiny speculative novelty ETF, more marketing than finance.
skepticChallenge.holds: Limits scale/durability, not the binary threshold — it's registered, listed, actively managed, funded. Scale belongs at rung 8.

rungs.title: Contractual risk transfer & hedging
rungs.oneLiner: No credible institutional UAP insurance, reinsurance, or derivative product.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Investment products give exposure; risk-transfer contracts require a counterparty to define triggers, exclusions, premiums, and assume a defined UAP loss.
rungs.statusRationale: No credible institutional UAP insurance/reinsurance/derivative, no UAP cat model, no parametric disclosure trigger. Novelty 'alien-abduction insurance' does not qualify. Generic all-risk cover that might respond regardless of cause is not UAP separately identified/priced.

rungs.title: Standards / audit / actuarial / ratings integration
rungs.oneLiner: No standard-setter, actuarial body, or rating agency has incorporated UAP exposure.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Bilateral products stay isolated; standards make multiple institutions use common definitions, materiality rules, and methodologies.
rungs.statusRationale: No UAP-specific record from IFRS/IASB/ISSB, FASB, SASB, SEC disclosure guidance, PCAOB/IAASB, the actuarial bodies, or Moody's/S&P/Fitch. Generic materiality/operational-risk rules could apply, but that is not engagement with UAP as a recognized category.

rungs.title: Routine market-wide incorporation
rungs.oneLiner: UAP absent from mainstream research, credit, insurance, corporate disclosure, standards.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Normalization endpoint — UAP routinely analysed, disclosed, priced and managed by multiple mainstream institutions, with observable market data. The 'widespread' state that rungs 1/3/5 (first-mover signals) point toward.
rungs.statusRationale: The record is one space ETF with a risk factor, one small disclosure ETF, and an old operating-company offering. No broad pattern across public-company risk factors, sell-side research, asset-allocation frameworks, credit ratings, insurance underwriting, audit, or regulatory guidance. No observable UAP risk premium.

excludedClaims.reason: Implausible proof requirements, no real risk-management role — not institutional risk transfer.

excludedClaims.claim: Meme coins / prediction-market bets on disclosure
excludedClaims.reason: Not institutional financial engagement; speculative novelty, outside the sector's risk/pricing functions.

excludedClaims.claim: A company merely mentioning UAP in passing
excludedClaims.reason: A mention is not recognition, governance, pricing, or a product — no rung crossed.

crossTrackNotes: Government appropriations and the congressional power of the purse are Legislative/Government, never here. Defense-contractor budgets are Military/Government. Academic/scientific funding is Scientific. This track is strictly the private financial/business sector's own acts.
